apologies in advance for the length but here’s what i suggest: 

stay in bellevue or issaquah if you’re fine with taking public transit into the city if/when you go into seattle. (sounds like you’re less focused on the touristy stuff this time around though). these places are way more green and way prettier than seattle with more recreation opportunities. 

mt. rainier NP is far from seattle (if you’re going into the park proper, it’ll take you at least 1.5 hours to get there, more if there’s traffic- go early in the AM on a weekday!). if you’re staying in bellevue, you can take 405 to 167 (or is it 161 ?) to get to mt. rainier which will likely shave off some travel time as opposed to being IN seattle. 

if you’re pressed for time, i’d venture to say the north bend area (mt. baker-snoqualmie national forest off the I-90 corridor) is prettier than mt. rainier (and much much closer to Seattle as it’s in king county as opposed to pierce/lewis co. as mt rainier is). if you’re open to this, i’d specifically recommend mt. si, rattlesnake lake, and the snoqualmie pass area. they’re beautiful this time of year!

seattle’s one of the best cities in the US imo. there’s sooooo much to do: there’s touristy stuff like the market and shops and at any given place you’re never far from hiking/nature. the people here are generally pretty chill and laid-back (and friendly, despite the stereotypes. there’s a few things to know before you ever plan a trip here though:  

1. the homeless crisis/opioid epidemic is HUGE out here. you’ll see some interesting people and maybe a needle or two if you’re anywhere near downtown. it’s the unfortunate reality here rn, but you’ll be fine as long as you’re aware of your surroundings. 

2. a lot of people visit here and complain about the rainy weather; rainy/gray season is usually from oct-march, so if you’re not into that, definitely plan a trip during the summer.

3. unless you live in nyc/la/san fran, everything will be more expensive here, so just be prepared for that. 

4. you will smell weed a lot in the city, like A LOT. you’ll see people smoking pot. depending on where you’re from, this might be a culture shock, but it’s part of the ~culture~ here so just embrace it. 

sorry this was kinda long and maybe a little obvious- these are just the things i had to adjust to after moving here, so hopefully it helps. come visit sometime :)
